confirmed: The complete markdown and all 9 PDF pages were read. The title, three authors, and source.version match arXiv:2507.08260v1, 11 Jul 2025; the PDF ends with references and contains no appendix (PDF p. 1, title block and arXiv stamp; pp. 8-9, References).

One online, within-person user study compares graph-based and conversational generative-AI interfaces. Half received each interface first, but the allocation mechanism is unstated; design_class other, randomized not_stated, and n_randomized null are supported (PDF p. 4, User Study and Study Design).

Eight people were recruited and included in the full questionnaire analysis, below the 50-person threshold. Both arm counts refer to the same participants, not separate samples or counts of writing outputs (PDF p. 4, User Study; p. 6, Participant Demographics and Table 1; p. 7, Limitations).

P4 could not use the graph interface but supplied questionnaire responses retained in the full analysis; the alternative analysis removes all of P4?s responses from both conditions, as the form describes (PDF p. 6, Results and Table 1; p. 8, Limitations).

The tasks were character descriptions or world-building, with different variants across interfaces and approximately 1:30-2 hours of participation. Both interfaces used OpenHermes-2.5-Mistral-7B and Stable Diffusion 2.1 (PDF pp. 4-5, User Study, Baseline and Additional Changes, and Study Design).

Questionnaire ratings concern satisfaction, perceived effect on the task answer, ease of use, and collaboration; qualitative themes concern participants? experiences. Example writing is reproduced without creativity or diversity scoring, so the empty outcomes array and criterion_3 not_met are supported (PDF pp. 5-7, Post-study questionnaire, Results, Tables 1-2, and Example Task Answers from P3).

The one-line finding?s ease-of-use means exactly match Table 1 with P4 included: Graph 2.875 and Chat 4.125. Higher scores mean easier use after the stated reversal; ideation benefits are participants? reports (PDF p. 5, footnote 4; p. 6, Table 1; p. 7, Table 2 and Discussion).

No qualifying randomized people study with output-scored creativity or diversity is documented. Core no and context_class none are supported by the unstated randomization, sub-50 sample, and questionnaire-only evaluation (PDF pp. 4-7, User Study through Results and Limitations).

This is an original system/user study, not a synthesis; there are no study-level reported strings or pooled estimates to verify, and the synthesis defaults are appropriate (PDF pp. 4-8, User Study through Conclusion).
summary: The form correctly excludes this eight-person study: interface-order randomization is unstated, and creativity or diversity was not scored on the writing. The version, counts, and ease-of-use means are confirmed; the sole correction is to fill the code URL explicitly provided in footnote 1.
